title: BLOCK-CUBE: block decoding saves one logarithm at the same fractional sample index

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single BLOCK-CUBE algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise m the least integer with m^3>=n, kappa=ceil(log2m)+1, base=ceil(n/(m+1)-m/2)+1, s0=kappa+1, dl=base+s0, H=base+m-1, L=floor(m/(4s0)), input widths base+i+min(s0,floor((m-1-i)s0/L)) and root target1, exact binary/radix/high-part implementation, Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), capped source/extraction and full bootstrap/signed-near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every execution branch total charged work O(n^(10/3)2^F(n)), including every gate, bit operation, lookup, address, source cost, initialization, reset and discarded attempt. Here F(n)=n^(2/3)-(1/2)n^(1/3), with the negative term explicit. The exact growth index is2/3. These are joint uniform envelopes; logarithmic envelopes at n=1 use their positive n=2 values. Finite exhaustive copies <=N(n+10) are absorbed only through outer constants; main guards apply only on the main branch. The generalized batch usesh unused top bits and exact block scoring withb0=floor(log2n),Lblk=ceil(n/b0); the entire odd and two-adic block decoder and reduced global acquisition cap are given in Sections9..13. All branch bounds remain joint.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
